The team played their home games at the [[McCarthey Athletic Center]], which has a capacity of 6,000. The Bulldogs (also informally referred to as the Zags), were in their 33rd season as a member of the [[West Coast Conference]], and were led by head coach [[Mark Few]], who was in his 14th season as head coach. In the [[2011–12 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|previous season]], the Zags gained a record of 26–7 and reached the third round of the [[2012 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2012 NCAA tournament]]. On March 4, 2013, Gonzaga was the top-ranked team in the nation for the first time in school history. The Bulldogs were the fifth team to be ranked number one during the 2013 (#) during NCAA Tournament is Seed with Region W=West}} ==Season== ===Preconference season=== [[File:20121112 Gonzaga Timeout During West Virginia Game.png|thumb|275px|right|Gonzaga takes a timeout during a non-conference game against [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]] on November 12, 2012]] The Gonzaga Bulldogs started their season with a 103–65 home win against [[Southern Utah Thunderbirds basketball|Southern Utah]] on November 9. They led Southern Utah at halftime 44–27, and started the second half with a 12–2 run. The Zags shot nearly 55 percent from the field, but only outrebounded the Thunderbirds 36–33. Freshman Przemek Karmowski led the Bulldogs with 22 points, while senior Guy Landri Edi scored a career-high 16 points.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=323142250|title=Freshman Przemek Karnowski scores 22 as Zags roll in opener|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=November 9, 2012|access-date=April 5, 2013}} Three days later, Gonzaga played [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]] as a part of the [[College Basketball on ESPN#Recent history|ESPN College Hoops Tip-Off Marathon]], where they would go on to rout the Mountaineers 84–50. They held West Virginia to 21 percent shooting in the first half, and led 45–18 at halftime. Matt Humphrey's steal and dunk cut Gonzaga's lead to 50–32 with 14:45 left, but [[Elias Harris]] responded with a three-pointer to push the lead back to 20. [[Gary Bell Jr.]] led the Bulldogs with 15 points, as four other players scored in double figures.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=323172250|title=Gary Bell Jr., Gonzaga heat up, shut down West Virginia|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=November 12, 2012|access-date=April 5, 2013}} On November 18, the Zags played at home against [[South Dakota Coyotes men's basketball|South Dakota]], where they would beat the Coyotes 96–58. Despite having 16 turnovers and making 4 of 15 free throws, the team outscored the Coyotes 38–9 in the [[Key (basketball)|paint]]. After a slow start, the Bulldogs went on an 18–4 run midway through the first half. Karnowski had a team-high 20 points, while Harris had 16 points and a career-high 18 rebounds in the victory.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=323232250|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171006013247/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=323232250|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 6, 2017|title=Elias Harris grabs 18 rebounds to lead Gonzaga's win|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=November 18, 2012|access-date=April 5, 2013}} During Thanksgiving weekend, the Bulldogs travelled to [[Lake Buena Vista, Florida]] to participate in the [[Old Spice Classic#2012 bracket|2012 Old Spice Classic]]. On November 22, Gonzaga went on to beat [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]] 57–49 in the first-round game of the tournament. After being behind by as much as eight, the Zags responded with the help of David Stockton, who had a career-high seven assists. [[Kelly Olynyk]], coming off of a [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] year, played in his first game of the season after being suspended for the previous three games for violating the student [[code of conduct]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=323272250|title=Elias Harris, Kelly Olynyk lead No. 17 Gonzaga past Clemson|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=November 22, 2012|access-date=April 5, 2013}} The next day, the Bulldogs went on to beat [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]] 72–47. The Sooners never had a lead in the game, as Harris scored 14 of his 18 points in the second half.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=323282250|title=Gonzaga defeats Oklahoma, headed to Old Spice Classic final|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=November 23, 2012|access-date=April 5, 2013}} In the Old Spice Classic championship game two days later, the Zags would hold on beat [[Davidson Wildcats men's basketball|Davidson]] 81–67 to capture its second tournament title and remain undefeated on the season at 6–0. After Davidson was ahead by as much as nine, [[Kevin Pangos]] connected on a three that made it 58–53 with eight minutes to play and scored another three two minutes later to make it 64–57. Harris finished with a team-high 24 points and 10 rebounds, while Pangos added 23 points, five assists, and two steals.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=323302250|title=Gonzaga tops Davidson to win Old Spice Classic championship|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=November 25, 2012|access-date=April 5, 2013}} The team returned home to play [[Lewis–Clark State College|Lewis-Clark State]] on November 29. They routed the Warriors 104–57, and were led by freshman Kyle Dranginis, who had a career-high 30 points, seven assists, and six rebounds. Despite sitting starters Harris and Bell, the Zags forced 20 turnovers and had a 46–20 rebounding advantage.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=323342250|title=Freshman Kyle Dranginis leads No. 12 Gonzaga over Lewis-Clark St.|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=November 29, 2012|access-date=April 5, 2013}} In the teams' first meeting since 1976, the Bulldogs defeated [[Pacific Tigers men's basketball|Pacific]] 85–67 two days later. Despite an early 18–10 Pacific lead, Gonzaga replied with a 10–0 run later in the first half to take a 49–34 halftime lead. The [[Basketball positions|frontcourt]] accounted for 64 of the team's points, as bench player Sam Dower scored 18 points and grabbed nine rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=323362250|title=Gonzaga ties team record for most wins to open season|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=December 1, 2012|access-date=April 5, 2013}} After this, the Zags faced their first true road game of the season as they travelled to play at [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]]. Down 67–69, DaVonte Lacy made a [[layup]] for the Cougars to tie the game. With the game tied at 69, Pangos drove up the court to make a layup with two seconds left to secure the 71–69 victory. Olynyk made 10 of 14 shots and grabbed seven rebounds to keep Gonzaga in the game in the second half, while Harris led the team with 23 points. The victory gave the Bulldogs their best start to a season in [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] history with a 9–0 record.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=323400265|title=Last-second layup lifts No. 10 Gonzaga over Washington State|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=December 5, 2012|access-date=April 5, 2013}} Gonzaga suffered their first loss of the season against #13 [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] on December 8, falling 85–74. Tied at 41 at halftime, the Zags shot 38 percent in the second half after shooting 60 percent in the first half. A free throw by Pangos cut Illinois' lead to 75–71 with 2:51 left in the game. However, the Illini responded with an 80–71 advantage to take control of the game.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=323432250|title=Brandon Paul's 35 power Illinois to win against Gonzaga|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=December 8, 2012|access-date=April 5, 2013}} The Bulldogs recovered from their first loss of the season by beating [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]] in the annual [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball#Battle in Seattle|State Farm Battle in Seattle]] game, 68–52. The team outscored Kansas State in the paint 38–12 and limited the Wildcats to 33 percent shooting. Olynyk led the team with 20 points, while Bell added 11 points.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=323502250|title=Kelly Olynyk dominates inside to power Gonzaga|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=December 15, 2012|access-date=April 5, 2013}} Four days later, Gonzaga returned home and beat [[Campbell Fighting Camels basketball|Campbell]] 74–52. The team finished with 33 points from the bench and 44 in the paint, while scoring 18 points off of 15 turnovers. Karnowski led the Zags with 14 points, while Harris put up 11 points and a career-high six assists.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=323542250|title=No. 14 Gonzaga tops Campbell as four players score in double figures|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=December 19, 2012|access-date=April 5, 2013}} With over a week to prepare for their next game at home, the Bulldogs beat [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] 94–87 on December 28. The team was unable to hold a lead until there was 4:53 remaining in the first half. At that point, the game went back and forth, and the Zags led by as many as 12. Pangos led the team with 31 points, while Olynyk and Harris added 21 and 17 points, respectively.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=323632250|title=Kevin Pangos erupts for 31, propels No. 13 Gonzaga by Baylor|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=December 28, 2012|access-date=April 5, 2013}} Gonzaga then went back on the road to play at #22 [[Oklahoma State Cowboys men's basketball|Oklahoma State]], where they got a 69–68 win. With 35.7 seconds left in the game, Mike Hart set a [[Screen (sports)|screen]] for Bell, who made a three-pointer to give the Zags the 67–65 lead. On the following play, Olynyk [[Personal foul (basketball)|fouled out]] and sent [[Marcus Smart]] to the free throw line. Smart missed both free throws and Pangos rebounded the ball, and subsequently was sent to the free throw line, where he made both free throws. The win made Gonzaga undefeated against the [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] for the season with a 5–0 record.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=323660197|title=Missed FTs doom No. 22 Oklahoma St. in loss to No. 10 Gonzaga|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=December 31, 2012|access-date=April 5, 2013}} ===Conference season=== [[File:20130202 Kelly Olynyk Drives Against Jito Kok.jpg|thumb|left|Gonzaga center [[Kelly Olynyk]] drives against Jito Kok in a conference game against [[San Diego Toreros men's basketball|San Diego]] on February 2, 2013]] To begin the conference season, the Bulldogs travelled to [[Firestone Fieldhouse]] on January 3 to play [[Pepperdine Waves men's basketball|Pepperdine]], where they would beat the Waves 78–62. David Stockton came off the bench and keyed the Zags with four steals to hold off a Pepperdine team that was down two with 12 minutes left. Despite scoring a season-low 43.4% from the field, Elias Harris scored 18 points and Kelly Olynyk added 16.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330032492|title=Elias Harris, Kelly Olynk send Gonzaga past Pepperdine|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=January 3, 2013|access-date=April 5, 2013}} Two days later, they went to [[Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball|Santa Clara]] and beat the Broncos 81–74. The team managed to withstand a Santa Clara rally late when Olynyk made a key putback with 1:55 remaining. He led the team with a career-high 33 points and 10 rebounds, while Harris added 14 points for the Zags.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330052541|title=Kelly Olynyk's career-best 33 helps Gonzaga survive|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=January 5, 2013|access-date=April 5, 2013}} After this, Gonzaga would go back home to play conference rival [[Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball|Saint Mary's]], whom they would beat 83–78. Saint Mary's would have one field goal in the final minutes of the first half to help the Bulldogs to a 46–28 halftime advantage. However, Stephen Holt would hit three shots and two free throws in a 90-second span to cut the lead to 55–44. With 26 seconds left, Kevin Pangos missed and fouled [[Matthew Dellavedova]], who made it 79–78. Gonzaga held on for the win and was led by 31 points from Olynyk.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330102250|title=Kelly Olynyk surpasses 30 again as No. 9 Zags roll|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=January 10, 2013|access-date=April 5, 2013}} On January 17, the Bulldogs went on the road to play [[Portland Pilots men's basketball|Portland]], whom they beat 71–49. Despite two early fouls on Olynyk in the first half, Gonzaga shot 46.6% from the field. Olynyk would come back with a strong second half to finish with 21 points, eight rebounds, one steal, and two blocks. The game extended Gonzaga's best start in school history with an eight-game winning streak.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330172501|title=No. 8 Gonzaga coasts past Portland, extends best-ever start|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=January 17, 2013|access-date=April 6, 2013}} Two days later, they would travel to [[Hinkle Fieldhouse]] to play a non-conference game at #13 [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]] as a part of the debut game of [[ESPN]]'s [[College GameDay (basketball)#2013|''College GameDay'']] for the [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2013 college basketball season]]. Gonzaga was ahead 33–32 at halftime, but Butler scored the first five points of the second half to take the lead. Ahead 63–62 with 3.5 seconds left, Stockton threw the ball inbounds and watched as it was stolen by Butler sophomore Roosevelt Jones, who took the [[Buzzer beater|buzzer beater shot]] to give Butler the 64–63 win.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330192086|title=Butler tops Gonzaga at buzzer thanks to Roosevelt Jones' steal, shot|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=January 19, 2013|access-date=April 6, 2013}} The team would recover and return home from their second loss of the season on January 24 by beating [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]] 83–63. Olynyk scored 26 points on 9-for-9 shooting and was also 8-for-8 on free throws. The Zags won the rebound battle 37–29 and outscored BYU 42–28 in the paint while shooting 56.9% from the field.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330242250|title=No. 10 Gonzaga rebounds from loss by trumping BYU|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=January 24, 2013|access-date=April 6, 2013}} Two days later, the team would go on to beat [[San Francisco Dons men's basketball|San Francisco]] at home 66–52. Despite shooting 58 percent in the first half and building a lead of 24 at one point, the Bulldogs shot just 8 of 27 in the second half. They were led by Olynyk, who had 13 points, eight rebounds, three assists, three steals, and one assist.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330262250|title=No. 10 Gonzaga extends home winning streak against San Fran|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=January 26, 2013|access-date=April 6, 2013}} The team then travelled to [[Loyola Marymount Lions men's basketball|Loyola Marymount]] on January 31, where they would rout the Lions 88–43. The team shot 13-for-21 from behind the three-point line and shot 54.4% from the field. Gary Bell Jr. led the team with 15 points, which were entirely three-pointers.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330312351|title=No. 7 Gonzaga pours in 13 3-pointers in rout of Loyola Marymount|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=January 31, 2013|access-date=April 6, 2013}} The team would face a tougher task when they went to [[San Diego Toreros men's basketball|San Diego]] two days later. The Zags left 36–27 at halftime, but San Diego would go on a run to drop the Gonzaga lead to 51–50. They trailed 57–53 with {{frac|7|1|2}} minutes left before outscoring the Toreros 12–6. Stockton would hit a runner in the lane with 55.9 seconds left, but Olynyk would miss the front end of a one-and-one to give San Diego a chance to win the game with eight seconds left. However, Harris would go on to block the last-second shot to secure the 65–63 victory. Harris scored 18 points and eight rebounds, while Olynyk and Bell added 15 and 13, respectively.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330330301|title=David Stockton's late runner helps Gonzaga ice San Diego|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=February 2, 2013|access-date=April 6, 2013}} The team would return home on February 7 to rout [[Pepperdine Waves men's basketball|Pepperdine]] 82–56. They managed to hold Pepperdine to 36.2% from the field and also forced 21 turnovers. Gonzaga was led by Kevin Pangos, who scored 14 points, collected four assists, and had four steals.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330382250|title=Kevin Pangos helps No. 6 Gonzaga pound Pepperdine|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=February 7, 2013|access-date=April 6, 2013}} Kelly Olynyk was key in the Zag's 74–55 home victory over [[Loyola Marymount Lions men's basketball|Loyola Marymount]] two days later. He scored 20 points, grabbed six rebounds, collected four assists, and had two blocks. Pangos also added 20 points, while Harris recorded a [[Double (basketball)|double-double]] with 16 points and 10 rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330402250|title=Kevin Pangos, No. 6 Gonzaga improve to 10-0 in WCC|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=February 9, 2013|access-date=April 6, 2013}} Gonzaga's next battle would take them down to [[Moraga, California]], where they would play the second conference game against rival [[Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball|Saint Mary's]]. Gaels point guard Matthew Dellavedova would score 19 of his 22 points in the first half, as the Gaels led the Zags 33–32 at the break. However, Gary Bell Jr. would go on to score 20 points and fuel a 7–0 run for the opening 1:06 of the second half to take the lead for good. The team managed to shoot 50% from the field, while converting 9 of 17 three-pointers. Pangos contributed 18 points and led the team with three assists, while Olynyk added 17 points to help the Zags take control of first place in the conference with an 11–0 record.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330452608|title=No. 5 Gonzaga downs rival Saint Mary's to take control of WCC|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=February 14, 2013|access-date=April 6, 2013}} The Zags then travelled to play [[San Francisco Dons men's basketball|San Francisco]] at [[War Memorial Gymnasium]], which is a place where they had not won for three consecutive years. Gonzaga's defense forced San Francisco to stay on the perimeter for a majority of their shots, as the Bulldogs limited the Dons to 36.8% from the field. Olynyk led the team with 26 points and nine rebounds, while Harris added 17 points and 13 rebounds to lead the team to a 71–61 victory.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330472539|title=Kelly Olynyk helps No. 5 Gonzaga down pesky San Francisco|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=February 16, 2013|access-date=April 6, 2013}} A rebounding advantage of 45–22 and defensive field goal percentage of 30.2% helped Gonzaga rout [[Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball|Santa Clara]] 85–42 on February 20. The Zags shot 56.2% from the field and converted on 7 of 17 three-pointers. Harris led the team with 17 points and nine rebounds, while Olynyk scored 15.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330512250|title=No. 3 Gonzaga drops Santa Clara, cruises to ninth straight win|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=February 20, 2013|access-date=April 6, 2013}} Three days later, the team beat [[San Diego Toreros men's basketball|San Diego]] at home 81–50. The team's defense held the Toreros to 35.7% shooting and 2-for-14 beyond the arc. Gonzaga came into the second half making its first six of seven shots to push the lead to 54–30 with 14 minutes left. After San Diego scored, transfer Drew Barham's three-pointer started a 13–0 Zags run that pushed the lead to 67–32. Pangos led the team with 18 points, while Olynyk contributed 14 points, nine rebounds, and three blocks.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330542250|title=Gonzaga on cusp of highest ranking after rout|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=February 23, 2013|access-date=April 6, 2013}} With two conference games left, the Bulldogs travelled to play at the [[Marriott Center]] against [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]] on February 28. The Zags led by 11 with 10:51 left in the game, but BYU would begin to cut the Gonzaga lead. Three three-pointers by Brock Zylstra and Craig Cusick, as well as two free throws by Brandon Davies tied the game at 60 with 4:18 remaining. Olynyk hit a key jumper with 43 seconds remaining and Pangos hit two free throws to give the Bulldogs some breathing room. However, Gonzaga fouled Cusick on a three-point attempt, causing him to make three free throws to give BYU one final chance with 6.6 seconds remaining. The Zags fouled BYU before Cusick could attempt a three, and Harris' free throws at the other end sealed Gonzaga's 70–65 victory.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330590252|title=No. 2 Gonzaga holds off BYU, assures itself top spot in WCC|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=February 28, 2013|access-date=April 6, 2013}} The final conference game of the season for the Zags would be at home against [[Portland Pilots men's basketball|Portland]] two days later, whom they would beat 81–52. Harris scored 20 points, while Olynyk grabbed a double-double with 15 points and 11 rebounds. The win made the team finish undefeated in conference play at 16–0 for the first time in team history and conference history. It also broke the team's [[2003–04 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|previous record]] for the best regular season start with 29 wins.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330612250|title=Gonzaga stakes claim to first No. 1 ranking after win over Portland|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=March 2, 2013|access-date=April 6, 2013}} ===Postseason=== On March 4, 2013, the team drew a number one ranking in both the [[AP Poll]] and [[Coaches' Poll]] for the first time in program history.{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/westcoast/2013/03/04/gonzaga-bulldogs-mark-few-top-ranking-coaches-poll/1960539/|title=Gonzaga earns first-ever No. 1 ranking, but spotlight 'nothing new'|last=Auerbach|first=Nicole|work=[[USA Today]]|publisher=[[Gannett Company]]|date=March 4, 2013|access-date=April 7, 2013}} In the [[2013 West Coast Conference men's basketball tournament]], the Bulldogs received a one seed by virtue of a 16–0 conference record, causing them to have a [[Bye (sports)|bye]] into the semifinals. Due to [[Loyola Marymount Lions men's basketball|Loyola Marymount]] beating [[Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball|Santa Clara]] in the quarterfinals, Gonzaga was matched up against Loyola Marymount. The team would go on to win the game 66–48, as they were led by Elias Harris, who had 21 points, eight rebounds, one assist, two steals, and two blocks.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330682250|title=Top-ranked Gonzaga cruises into WCC final|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=March 9, 2013|access-date=April 7, 2013}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} In the championship game of the tournament, the Zags would go against rival [[Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball|Saint Mary's]] for the third time. The defense of the Bulldogs forced Saint Mary's guard Matthew Dellavedova to score two points on 1 of 8 shooting and have the Gaels shoot 35.7% from the field as a whole. The team shot 52.1% from the field and dominated the Gaels in the paint 42–18. The Zags were led by Kelly Olynyk, who contributed 21 points and 12 rebounds. Harris also added 19 points for the Bulldogs, and would later be named the [[Most Valuable Player|MVP]] of the tournament. With the victory, the Bulldogs secured an [[automatic bid]] into the [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2013 NCAA tournament]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330702250|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210918232343/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330702250|url-status=dead|archive-date=September seasons before, the Jaguars were only behind 34–31 at halftime. Olynyk scored 17 of his 21 points in the second half to help Gonzaga pull ahead. Despite this, Southern managed to tie the game at 56 with 3:45 left, but Gary Bell Jr. would hit a three-pointer to make it 59–56. On the ensuing possession, Southern guard Derick Beltran hit two free throws to cut the deficit to one. However, Kevin Pangos would respond with a three-pointer to put the Zags ahead by four. YonDarius Johnson and Malcolm Miller had open looks on the next possession, but neither was able to convert. Pangos finished with 16 points and hit two free throws with 14.3 seconds left to seal the victory for Gonzaga. The team managed to avoid the upset and hold on for the 64–58 victory to advance to the Round of 32.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330802250|title=Top-seeded Gonzaga survives upset bid by pesky Southern|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=March 21, 2013|access-date=April 7, 2013}} Gonzaga's season came to an end on March 21 with a 76–70 loss to ninth-seeded [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]]. The Shockers had a 36–31 lead at halftime, and were ahead by as much as 13 at one point in the game. However, the Bulldogs would respond with a 12–0 run in the second half to give themselves a 49–41 lead with 11:53 left. Nevertheless, Wichita State started a string of five straight three-pointers when Tekele Cotton hit one with 6:05 remaining, cutting the deficit to four. With 1:28 seconds left, [[Fred VanVleet]] threw up and converted on a three-pointer with one second left on the [[shot clock]] to give the Shockers a 70–65 lead. The rest of the game was a free throw shooting contest, as Wichita State shot 50% from the field and 50% from beyond the arc, converting on 14 of 28 attempts from long range. Olynyk contributed 26 points and 9 rebounds, while Pangos scored 19. The loss made the Zags the first number one seed to be eliminated as they finished with a record of 32–3.{{cite
